<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation

<!-- Describe the purpose and goals of this pull request. -->

SGLang's Mooncake HiCache backend currently relies on Mooncake's default
replica placement. It does not expose request-level controls for memory or
descriptor-based DFS replicas, so deployments cannot request additional memory
replicas or evaluate Mooncake's DFS replica path through the standard HiCache
configuration.

This PR exposes Mooncake replica placement through the HiCache backend while
preserving the existing default behavior.

## Modifications

<!-- Detail the changes made in this pull request. -->

- Add `replica_num` and `dfs_replica_num` to
  `--hicache-storage-backend-extra-config`, with defaults of `1` and `0`.
- Create a request-scoped `ReplicateConfig` for standard and multi-buffer
  writes, and compose it with the existing `group_ids` setting.
- Validate replica counts and reject Mooncake versions that do not expose the
  requested configuration fields.
- Fail fast when embedded DFS mode is missing SSD offload, the distributed
  storage backend descriptor, or an absolute storage path.
- Keep standalone Dummy Client mode compatible with replica configuration
  owned by the external Real Client.
- Document embedded and standalone DFS setup and the current experimental
  limitations.
- Add unit coverage for validation, compatibility, request isolation, group
  semantics, and multi-buffer writes.

The default configuration continues to use the existing three-argument
`batch_put_from` path.

### Functional Tests

The focused unit tests passed:

```bash
pytest -q \
  test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_mooncake_group_semantics.py \
  test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_mooncake_standalone_dummy_mamba.py
```

```text
22 passed, 6 subtests passed
```

A local end-to-end test also passed on an NVIDIA A100 with
`Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct`, using Mooncake's POSIX DFS adapter and
`replica_num=1, dfs_replica_num=1`:

- The initial 768-token request reported `cached_tokens=0`.
- After the write, the four sparse DFS shards grew from 0 to 9,445,376 bytes
  of allocated storage.
- After flushing SGLang's device cache, replaying the same request reported
  `cached_tokens=704` (11 pages with `page_size=64`).
- Mooncake master logs reported `Replica #2: dfs_file=...`, confirming that
  the second replica was placed in POSIX DFS rather than only in memory.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

nodes.body:
Thanks for this PR — it's exactly the integration needed now that Mooncake merged DFS-only replica placement ([kvcache-ai/Mooncake#4637](https://github.com/kvcache-ai/Mooncake/pull/4637)).

I validated the DFS-only configuration (`replica_num=0, dfs_replica_num=1`, with this PR's extra-config) on top of its snapshot (`1cbab10`). Sharing the measurements plus three local patches it took to make DFS-only work, in case they're useful for review.

### Setup

Single node with 8× NVIDIA H100 80GB, SGLang v0.5.21 image, Mooncake #4637 snapshot (source-built wheel), Qwen3.5-397B-FP8 TP8, multiturn cache-reuse workload — 40 concurrent clients, 10 rounds each where every client re-sends its own ~77K-token prompt with a new 5K-token sub-question per round (so rounds 1+ exercise the L2/L3 hit path), Poisson arrivals at rate 0.8, 1K-token outputs. 3 reps with full cold restart between reps (L1+L2+L3 all cleared). L3 = Mooncake POSIX DFS adapter, 64 × 10 GB shards on a local NVMe SSD, zero memory segments mounted.

### Finding: `DEFAULT_LOCAL_BUFFER_SIZE = 16 MB` starves DFS reads

DFS/DISK replica reads stage through the client buffer allocator (`real_client.cpp` — temp buffer → scatter to destination). With the hardcoded 16 MB default, read allocation failed 845,248 times over a 3-rep benchmark (512 KB page requests), so nearly all prefetches were dropped:

| `local_buffer_size` | read alloc failures | avg cache hit | mean TTFT |
|---|---|---|---|
| (no L3 — L2-only baseline) | n/a | 50.4% | 14.2 s |
| 16 MB (current default) | 845,248 / run | 56.6% | 13.9 s |
| 2 GB | ~14K / run | 78.5% | 2.35 s |
| 16 GB | 0 | **80.6%** | **2.34 s** |

The 16 MB default looks tuned for the zero-copy write path only ("Zero copy interface does not need local buffer"). Memory-replica reads don't use this staging path, which is likely why the PR's `replica_num=1, dfs_replica_num=1` E2E didn't surface it — it only bites when DFS/DISK replicas serve reads.

### Two categories of local changes I needed

**A. To make DFS-only work at all (correctness):**

1. **Allow `(replica_num=0, dfs_replica_num=1)`** — currently rejected by `replica_num must be at least 1`. Mooncake #4637 explicitly supports this placement now (it's the object's only copy; DFS eviction/removal deletes it).
2. **The startup warmup must use the placement config** — `MooncakeStore.warmup()` (a dummy-object liveness check at store init) currently does a default 2-arg `store.put`, which requests a memory replica and fails on zero-segment setups. It needs the same `ReplicateConfig` as normal writes. (Related: passing `None` as the third arg raises a pybind11 `TypeError` — the default path must keep the 2-arg form.)

**B. To make it fast (performance):**

3. **`local_buffer_size` as an extra-config option** instead of the hardcoded 16 MB — this is the finding above. Without it DFS-only *works* but reads are starved (hit 56.6%, effectively close to the L2-only baseline).

With all three: DFS-only runs end-to-end — 677K objects / 582 GB written with zero `insufficient space`, and hit rate 80.6% vs the 50.4% L2-only baseline (+30.2 pp from the DFS tier once reads aren't starved).

One operational note: with zero memory segments, the master's `/get_all_segments` returns an empty body, so `check_server` never succeeds — `check_server: false` plus warmup-based readiness works.

Of these, (B) and the `None` TypeError fix are placement-independent. The buffer-size issue in particular applies to any DISK/DFS replica read staged through the client buffer allocator — not just this PR's placement — so it may be worth fixing even outside this PR's scope. @huangtingwei9988 would a small standalone PR for `local_buffer_size` exposure (plus the warmup `None` fix) against main make sense here, or would you prefer it folded into this PR? And if you're short on cycles, glad to take over the remaining work here.

Thanks @wooyeonlee0 for the detailed validation and measurements!

@wooyeonlee0 @huangtingwei9988 I've folded the changes into this PR as three separate commits:

- 6eb2f6f: Allow DFS-only placement and use the requested replica configuration during warmup. The default path keeps the two-argument put() call without passing None.
- 7a0fb88: Expose local_buffer_size through extra-config, accepting byte counts or strings such as "1gb", while preserving the 16 MiB default.
- ba29f0e: Update the deployment docs, including check_server=false for zero-memory-segment setups and buffer sizing guidance.

The docs also clarify that standalone deployments must configure the external Real Client's DFS staging buffer separately.

Focused CPU tests passed: 30 tests and 17 subtests, with unrelated inference/metrics imports isolated. Pre-commit passed on all changed files. I haven't rerun the real Mooncake/GPU E2E on this revision.

@huangtingwei9988 The buffer change is isolated in its own commit if you'd prefer to split it into a standalone PR. @wooyeonlee0 If you have a chance to rerun your workload against this head, that would help validate the DFS read path.

To follow up on your request — I reran the full workload against this head (`6592d38`), and the DFS read path works well. Results below.

### Setup

Same setup as in my [earlier comment](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/37390#issuecomment-6309132832), except where noted:

- **Changed — this head's `mooncake_store.py`** (`6592d38`) replaces my local patch; everything else in the SGLang side is identical
- Hardware: single node, 8× H100 80GB (different node than the earlier run — dsrh100-021)
- Model: Qwen3.5-397B-FP8, TP8, EAGLE (3 steps / topk 1 / 4 draft tokens), `mem_fraction_static` 0.79, `max_running_requests` 32, page 64
- L2: `hicache_ratio` 2.8, write-through-selective
- Workload: v2-style multiturn cache-reuse — 40 clients × 10 rounds re-sending ~77K-token prompts with a new 5K sub-question per round, Poisson rate 0.8, 3 reps with full cold restart between reps
- L3: Mooncake [kvcache-ai/Mooncake#4637](https://github.com/kvcache-ai/Mooncake/pull/4637) snapshot source-built wheel, DFS-only (`replica_num=0, dfs_replica_num=1`, zero memory segments), POSIX DFS adapter (64 × 10GB shards on local NVMe)
- `local_buffer_size` set to **16 GB** — server log confirms `Registering local memory: 17179869184 bytes`

### Results on this head (dsrh100-021, 3-rep)

| Metric | DFS-only (this head) | L2-only (no L3) |
|---|---|---|
| avg cache hit | **85.8% ± 0.5** | 50.4% |
| mean TTFT | **2.36s ± 0.16** | 14.2s |
| TTFT p90 / p99 | 6.77s / 18.6s | 42.5s / 81.8s |
| read alloc failures | 0 across all reps | n/a |
| request success | 400 / 400 per rep, all 30/30 rounds | — |
| ITL p99 | 317.7 ms | — |

L2-only is the no-L3 baseline for the same workload and cold-restart contract — the DFS tier contributes +35.4 pp of cache hit and a 6× mean-TTFT improvement, with decode unaffected (ITL p99 unchanged).

The read path is heavily exercised, not just spot-checked: master key count grows 8 → ~821K over a rep, prefetch reports pages loaded (not just matched), and per-rep I/O volume is **~1 TB written / ~1.7 TB read** (page counters × 64-token pages × ~16 KB/token).

Thanks for folding in the changes so quickly — the GB-string parsing and `setup_dummy` propagation are nice touches beyond my local patch, and nice to see this connect to your Mooncake-side [DFS replica POSIX backend](https://github.com/kvcache-ai/Mooncake/pull/2683) as well.

I also have a 3FS (hf3fs) comparison from two separate 3-rep sessions on the same node — DFS-only came out ahead on TTFT in both:

| Backend | hit | mean TTFT |
|---|---|---|
| **DFS-only (this head, 10-23)** | 85.8% ± 0.5 | **2.36s ± 0.16** |
| 3FS (10-23, same day) | 78.8% ± 1.3 | 12.17s ± 1.08 |
| 3FS (10-16, separate cluster build) | 87.1% ± 0.5 | 5.03s |

Across both sessions, TTFT favored DFS-only — even when 3FS hit a higher cache rate. That's unexpected for us since the DFS path is POSIX-based while 3FS uses USRBIO, but both sessions are internally consistent (3 reps each).

We're evaluating the DFS-only path for our serving stack and looking forward to this landing. One practical note: no Mooncake release contains [kvcache-ai/Mooncake#4637](https://github.com/kvcache-ai/Mooncake/pull/4637) yet, so I'm on a source-built wheel — @fcczzz if you know when the next release might include it, that would help us plan. Happy to run more workloads or share raw data meanwhile.

@wooyeonlee0 Thanks for rerunning the full workload and sharing these results! It's great to see the DFS-only read path working well with the updated code.

We're targeting a new Mooncake release next week that includes DFS-only placement support from #4637, so you should no longer need a source-built wheel once it's available. The timing is tentative, but that's our current plan.

files.patch:
@@ -303,6 +303,96 @@ You can enable it in any of the three supported configuration methods:
 
 > **Note:** `enable_ssd_offload` requires a Mooncake version that supports the `enable_ssd_offload` parameter in `MooncakeDistributedStore.setup()`. If the installed version does not support it, SGLang will automatically fall back to the old behavior and print a warning.
 
+**Mooncake Replica Placement (`replica_num`, `dfs_replica_num`):**
+
+> **Warning:** Descriptor-based DFS is a work-in-progress feature intended only
+> for development and evaluation. It is not covered by Mooncake's production
+> fault-tolerance, HA, durability, or multi-tenant guarantees. In particular,
+> DFS allocator state is not reconstructed after a master restart or HA
+> failover, and DFS writes currently have no DFS-specific timeout,
+> cancellation, or `fsync` durability guarantee. See the
+> [Mooncake descriptor-based DFS documentation](https://github.com/kvcache-ai/Mooncake/blob/main/docs/source/deployment/mooncake-store-deployment-guide.md#descriptor-based-dfs-storage)
+> for the current limitations.
+
+Use `replica_num` and `dfs_replica_num` in
+`--hicache-storage-backend-extra-config` to control the number of memory and
+descriptor-based DFS replicas created for each HiCache object. The defaults are
+`1` and `0`, respectively. `replica_num` must be non-negative,
+`dfs_replica_num` must be `0` or `1`, and at least one replica is required.
+DFS-only placement (`replica_num=0`, `dfs_replica_num=1`) requires a Mooncake
+version that includes [DFS-only replica support](https://github.com/kvcache-ai/Mooncake/pull/4637).
+The following example uses one memory replica and one DFS replica in the
+default embedded Real Client mode:
+
+```bash
+python -m sglang.launch_server \
+    --enable-hierarchical-cache \
+    --hicache-storage-backend mooncake \
+    --model-path [model_path] \
+    --hicache-storage-backend-extra-config \
+    '{"master_server_address":"127.0.0.1:50051","replica_num":1,"dfs_replica_num":1,"enable_ssd_offload":true,"ssd_offload_path":"/tmp/mooncake-file-storage"}'
+```
+
+Descriptor-based DFS currently requires the default Mooncake tenant. Start the
+Mooncake master with `MOONCAKE_ENABLE_DFS=1`, and configure the master and every
+Real Client with the same `MOONCAKE_DFS_*` layout. Although DFS data is written
+under `MOONCAKE_DFS_ROOT_DIR`, each Real Client must also initialize FileStorage
+with the distributed backend and an existing absolute file-storage path.
+
+In the default embedded Real Client mode, the Real Client runs inside SGLang.
+Set `MOONCAKE_OFFLOAD_STORAGE_BACKEND_DESCRIPTOR=distributed_storage_backend`
+in the SGLang process, and pass `enable_ssd_offload=true` plus an absolute
+`ssd_offload_path` as shown above.
+
+With `standalone_storage=true`, SGLang runs only a Dummy Client. Configure the
+external `mooncake_client` process instead: set the same `MOONCAKE_DFS_*`
+layout,
+`MOONCAKE_OFFLOAD_STORAGE_BACKEND_DESCRIPTOR=distributed_storage_backend`,
+`MOONCAKE_OFFLOAD_ENABLED=true`, and an absolute
+`MOONCAKE_OFFLOAD_FILE_STORAGE_PATH`. SGLang only needs `replica_num`,
+`dfs_replica_num`, `standalone_storage=true`, and `client_server_address`; the
+Dummy Client forwards the request-level replica configuration to the external
+Real Client.
+
+For an embedded DFS-only client that contributes no memory segment, use:
+
+```bash
+python -m sglang.launch_server \
+    --enable-hierarchical-cache \
+    --hicache-storage-backend mooncake \
+    --model-path [model_path] \
+    --hicache-storage-backend-extra-config \
+    '{"master_server_address":"127.0.0.1:50051","replica_num":0,"dfs_replica_num":1,"global_segment_size":0,"check_server":false,"local_buffer_size":"1gb","enable_ssd_offload":true,"ssd_offload_path":"/tmp/mooncake-file-storage"}'
+```
+
+The DFS environment and file-storage path requirements above still apply.
+When the deployment has no memory segments, set `check_server=false`: the
+segment-list readiness check cannot establish readiness from an empty list.
+The startup warmup instead writes and reads a test object using the requested
+replica placement. In standalone mode, also configure the external Real Client
+without memory segments if the entire deployment should be DFS-only.
+
+**Client Read Buffer (`local_buffer_size`):**
+
+Set `local_buffer_size` in `--hicache-storage-backend-extra-config` to size the
+Mooncake client's scratch buffer. It accepts a positive integer byte count, a
+string containing that count, or an integer GB string such as `"1gb"` (1 GiB).
+The default remains 16 MiB. This is a per-rank setting and is not divided by
+TP or PP size.
+
+In embedded mode, DFS and DISK reads stage data in this buffer before copying
+it to the HiCache host pool. Size it for the object sizes, batch sizes, and
+concurrent reads in your workload; insufficient capacity causes read allocation
+failures. The 1 GiB value above is an example, not a universal sizing requirement.
+A memory-plus-DFS test may read the memory replica, so validate DFS reads with
+DFS-only placement or after making the memory replica unavailable.
+
+In standalone mode, SGLang forwards this setting to `setup_dummy()` for the
+Dummy Client's scratch buffer. DFS read staging occurs in the external Real
+Client, whose `local_buffer_size` must be configured separately. The
+FileStorage restore buffer used by ordinary SSD offload is also a separate
+buffer; this option does not resize it.
+
 **Mooncake Group Semantics (`enable_group_semantics`):**
 
 When `enable_group_semantics` is set to `true`, SGLang passes Mooncake `group_ids` for physical objects derived from the same logical HiCache page. This allows Mooncake to apply group-aware metadata routing, lease refresh, and eviction behavior to related KV objects such as MHA K/V pairs, split-head shards, MLA objects, and supported sidecar objects.

@@ -84,13 +84,34 @@ def _parse_global_segment_size(value) -> int:
     return int(value)
 
 
+def _parse_local_buffer_size(value: Any) -> int:
+    message = (
+        "Mooncake local_buffer_size must be a positive integer in bytes or a GB string"
+    )
+    if isinstance(value, bool) or not isinstance(value, (int, str)):
+        raise ValueError(message)
+    try:
+        size = _parse_global_segment_size(value)
+    except ValueError as exc:
+        raise ValueError(message) from exc
+    if size <= 0:
+        raise ValueError(message)
+    return size
+
+
 def _normalize_tenant_id(value) -> str:
     if value is None:
         return DEFAULT_TENANT_ID
     tenant_id = str(value).strip()
     return tenant_id if tenant_id else DEFAULT_TENANT_ID
 
 
+def _parse_replica_count(name: str, value: Any) -> int:
+    if isinstance(value, bool) or not isinstance(value, int):
+        raise ValueError(f"Mooncake {name} must be an integer")
+    return value
+
+
 @dataclass
 class MooncakeStoreConfig:
     local_hostname: str
@@ -403,6 +424,82 @@ def __init__(
                 if storage_config
                 else None
             )
+            self.local_buffer_size = _parse_local_buffer_size(
+                extra_config.get("local_buffer_size", DEFAULT_LOCAL_BUFFER_SIZE)
+                if extra_config
+                else DEFAULT_LOCAL_BUFFER_SIZE
+            )
+            self.replica_num = _parse_replica_count(
+                "replica_num",
+                extra_config.get("replica_num", 1) if extra_config else 1,
+            )
+            self.dfs_replica_num = _parse_replica_count(
+                "dfs_replica_num",
+                extra_config.get("dfs_replica_num", 0) if extra_config else 0,
+            )

Thanks for this PR — it's exactly the integration needed now that Mooncake merged DFS-only replica placement ([kvcache-ai/Mooncake#4637](https://github.com/kvcache-ai/Mooncake/pull/4637)).

I validated the DFS-only configuration (`replica_num=0, dfs_replica_num=1`, with this PR's extra-config) on top of its snapshot (`1cbab10`). Sharing the measurements plus three local patches it took to make DFS-only work, in case they're useful for review.

### Setup

Single node with 8× NVIDIA H100 80GB, SGLang v0.5.21 image, Mooncake #4637 snapshot (source-built wheel), Qwen3.5-397B-FP8 TP8, multiturn cache-reuse workload — 40 concurrent clients, 10 rounds each where every client re-sends its own ~77K-token prompt with a new 5K-token sub-question per round (so rounds 1+ exercise the L2/L3 hit path), Poisson arrivals at rate 0.8, 1K-token outputs. 3 reps with full cold restart between reps (L1+L2+L3 all cleared). L3 = Mooncake POSIX DFS adapter, 64 × 10 GB shards on a local NVMe SSD, zero memory segments mounted.

### Finding: `DEFAULT_LOCAL_BUFFER_SIZE = 16 MB` starves DFS reads

DFS/DISK replica reads stage through the client buffer allocator (`real_client.cpp` — temp buffer → scatter to destination). With the hardcoded 16 MB default, read allocation failed 845,248 times over a 3-rep benchmark (512 KB page requests), so nearly all prefetches were dropped:

| `local_buffer_size` | read alloc failures | avg cache hit | mean TTFT |
|---|---|---|---|
| (no L3 — L2-only baseline) | n/a | 50.4% | 14.2 s |
| 16 MB (current default) | 845,248 / run | 56.6% | 13.9 s |
| 2 GB | ~14K / run | 78.5% | 2.35 s |
| 16 GB | 0 | **80.6%** | **2.34 s** |

The 16 MB default looks tuned for the zero-copy write path only ("Zero copy interface does not need local buffer"). Memory-replica reads don't use this staging path, which is likely why the PR's `replica_num=1, dfs_replica_num=1` E2E didn't surface it — it only bites when DFS/DISK replicas serve reads.

### Two categories of local changes I needed

**A. To make DFS-only work at all (correctness):**

1. **Allow `(replica_num=0, dfs_replica_num=1)`** — currently rejected by `replica_num must be at least 1`. Mooncake #4637 explicitly supports this placement now (it's the object's only copy; DFS eviction/removal deletes it).
2. **The startup warmup must use the placement config** — `MooncakeStore.warmup()` (a dummy-object liveness check at store init) currently does a default 2-arg `store.put`, which requests a memory replica and fails on zero-segment setups. It needs the same `ReplicateConfig` as normal writes. (Related: passing `None` as the third arg raises a pybind11 `TypeError` — the default path must keep the 2-arg form.)

**B. To make it fast (performance):**

3. **`local_buffer_size` as an extra-config option** instead of the hardcoded 16 MB — this is the finding above. Without it DFS-only *works* but reads are starved (hit 56.6%, effectively close to the L2-only baseline).

With all three: DFS-only runs end-to-end — 677K objects / 582 GB written with zero `insufficient space`, and hit rate 80.6% vs the 50.4% L2-only baseline (+30.2 pp from the DFS tier once reads aren't starved).

One operational note: with zero memory segments, the master's `/get_all_segments` returns an empty body, so `check_server` never succeeds — `check_server: false` plus warmup-based readiness works.

Of these, (B) and the `None` TypeError fix are placement-independent. The buffer-size issue in particular applies to any DISK/DFS replica read staged through the client buffer allocator — not just this PR's placement — so it may be worth fixing even outside this PR's scope. @huangtingwei9988 would a small standalone PR for `local_buffer_size` exposure (plus the warmup `None` fix) against main make sense here, or would you prefer it folded into this PR? And if you're short on cycles, glad to take over the remaining work here.

Thanks @wooyeonlee0 for the detailed validation and measurements!

@wooyeonlee0 @huangtingwei9988 I've folded the changes into this PR as three separate commits:

- 6eb2f6f: Allow DFS-only placement and use the requested replica configuration during warmup. The default path keeps the two-argument put() call without passing None.
- 7a0fb88: Expose local_buffer_size through extra-config, accepting byte counts or strings such as "1gb", while preserving the 16 MiB default.
- ba29f0e: Update the deployment docs, including check_server=false for zero-memory-segment setups and buffer sizing guidance.

The docs also clarify that standalone deployments must configure the external Real Client's DFS staging buffer separately.

Focused CPU tests passed: 30 tests and 17 subtests, with unrelated inference/metrics imports isolated. Pre-commit passed on all changed files. I haven't rerun the real Mooncake/GPU E2E on this revision.

@huangtingwei9988 The buffer change is isolated in its own commit if you'd prefer to split it into a standalone PR. @wooyeonlee0 If you have a chance to rerun your workload against this head, that would help validate the DFS read path.

To follow up on your request — I reran the full workload against this head (`6592d38`), and the DFS read path works well. Results below.

### Setup

Same setup as in my [earlier comment](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/37390#issuecomment-6309132832), except where noted:

- **Changed — this head's `mooncake_store.py`** (`6592d38`) replaces my local patch; everything else in the SGLang side is identical
- Hardware: single node, 8× H100 80GB (different node than the earlier run — dsrh100-021)
- Model: Qwen3.5-397B-FP8, TP8, EAGLE (3 steps / topk 1 / 4 draft tokens), `mem_fraction_static` 0.79, `max_running_requests` 32, page 64
- L2: `hicache_ratio` 2.8, write-through-selective
- Workload: v2-style multiturn cache-reuse — 40 clients × 10 rounds re-sending ~77K-token prompts with a new 5K sub-question per round, Poisson rate 0.8, 3 reps with full cold restart between reps
- L3: Mooncake [kvcache-ai/Mooncake#4637](https://github.com/kvcache-ai/Mooncake/pull/4637) snapshot source-built wheel, DFS-only (`replica_num=0, dfs_replica_num=1`, zero memory segments), POSIX DFS adapter (64 × 10GB shards on local NVMe)
- `local_buffer_size` set to **16 GB** — server log confirms `Registering local memory: 17179869184 bytes`

### Results on this head (dsrh100-021, 3-rep)

| Metric | DFS-only (this head) | L2-only (no L3) |
|---|---|---|
| avg cache hit | **85.8% ± 0.5** | 50.4% |
| mean TTFT | **2.36s ± 0.16** | 14.2s |
| TTFT p90 / p99 | 6.77s / 18.6s | 42.5s / 81.8s |
| read alloc failures | 0 across all reps | n/a |
| request success | 400 / 400 per rep, all 30/30 rounds | — |
| ITL p99 | 317.7 ms | — |

L2-only is the no-L3 baseline for the same workload and cold-restart contract — the DFS tier contributes +35.4 pp of cache hit and a 6× mean-TTFT improvement, with decode unaffected (ITL p99 unchanged).

The read path is heavily exercised, not just spot-checked: master key count grows 8 → ~821K over a rep, prefetch reports pages loaded (not just matched), and per-rep I/O volume is **~1 TB written / ~1.7 TB read** (page counters × 64-token pages × ~16 KB/token).

Thanks for folding in the changes so quickly — the GB-string parsing and `setup_dummy` propagation are nice touches beyond my local patch, and nice to see this connect to your Mooncake-side [DFS replica POSIX backend](https://github.com/kvcache-ai/Mooncake/pull/2683) as well.

I also have a 3FS (hf3fs) comparison from two separate 3-rep sessions on the same node — DFS-only came out ahead on TTFT in both:

| Backend | hit | mean TTFT |
|---|---|---|
| **DFS-only (this head, 10-23)** | 85.8% ± 0.5 | **2.36s ± 0.16** |
| 3FS (10-23, same day) | 78.8% ± 1.3 | 12.17s ± 1.08 |
| 3FS (10-16, separate cluster build) | 87.1% ± 0.5 | 5.03s |

Across both sessions, TTFT favored DFS-only — even when 3FS hit a higher cache rate. That's unexpected for us since the DFS path is POSIX-based while 3FS uses USRBIO, but both sessions are internally consistent (3 reps each).

We're evaluating the DFS-only path for our serving stack and looking forward to this landing. One practical note: no Mooncake release contains [kvcache-ai/Mooncake#4637](https://github.com/kvcache-ai/Mooncake/pull/4637) yet, so I'm on a source-built wheel — @fcczzz if you know when the next release might include it, that would help us plan. Happy to run more workloads or share raw data meanwhile.

@wooyeonlee0 Thanks for rerunning the full workload and sharing these results! It's great to see the DFS-only read path working well with the updated code.

We're targeting a new Mooncake release next week that includes DFS-only placement support from #4637, so you should no longer need a source-built wheel once it's available. The timing is tentative, but that's our current plan.
